articles.title: Health is wealth? Polymarket and Kalshi now host bets on measles and other US health crises
articles.summary:
Experts warn of risks of platforms hosting bets tied to US public health – including vaccine mandates and drug trials

The sign was pasted on a construction fence next to an elementary school…

blocks.text: The sign was pasted on a construction fence next to an elementary school in the Brooklyn borough of New York City. “Vaccines,” it proclaimed in bold capital letters against a blue star-spangled background – appearing, at first glance, to be like any other public health message on the importance of getting vaccinated.

But at the bottom of the sign, in smaller letters, it read: “Will any state end vaccine markets?” It was accompanied by the logo for Polymarket, an online prediction market where users can log in to wager on the outcomes of nearly any event – including, now, public health.

Polymarket joins Kalshi, another online prediction market, which began offering health-related predictions over the summer. Users can wager on when the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will approve a skin-cancer vaccine, or whether the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will change its vaccine recommendations. They can also bet on drug trial outcomes and approval; they can bet on how many cases of measles the US might see in 2026 and whether it will lose its measles-elimination status this year.

“I am not surprised,” said Matthew Eisenberg, professor and chair of health policy and management at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. “Kalshi and Polymarket will list contracts on anything with a checkable outcome.”

Despite being functionally “identical” to regulated gambling, prediction markets are largely unregulated, said Lia Nower, a professor and the director of the Center for Gambling Studies at Rutgers University.

“Gambling right now is like the wild, wild west,” she added. “There’s no federal regulatory body that’s really prescribing any limits on any of this, or just minimum guidelines for states to follow – so anything’s possible.”

Prediction markets position themselves as financial derivatives, rather than traditional bets, in a regulatory loophole, Nower said – which means they operate under federal commodities laws, with oversight from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and are not regulated by states as gambling operations. Several states have filed lawsuits against the companies alleging that they function as gambling sites.

Advocates, officials and lawmakers could place bets on ending vaccine mandates at the state level, for instance, and then introduce new laws or policies to do so; there don’t appear to be any laws against that, Nower said. There are bets on when certain officials will leave health agencies, which could be affected by resignation or termination decisions.

Predictions could also affect how drugs are tested and regulated, critics say. Trial participants could purposefully change their behavior to affect outcomes; drug companies could change the timing of trials.

Predictions on FDA decisions and trial endpoints “create a payoff for anyone with nonpublic information”, like agency reviewers, trial investigators and legislative staff, Eisenberg said. Prediction markets may create their own safeguards, like employment checks at sign-up, “but the risk isn’t necessarily that a reviewer takes a bribe – it’s that the market now rewards leaks”, he said.

Polymarket did not respond to the Guardian’s questions about the potential consequences for public health or medicine. Kalshi did not respond on the record to the same questions, but spokesperson Dani Lever argued that the predictions on drug trials and approvals would improve transparency.

“Kalshi’s clinical trial markets are a pilot program aimed at a structural problem in drug development: the people who best know whether a trial will succeed are scattered, and their insight rarely reaches the public,” Lever said in a statement. “Public markets avoid those barriers.”
Problem gambling is itself a rapidly growing public health concern.

Gambling is a “big public health issue” that disproportionately affects people who are younger, Black or Hispanic and lower-income, Nower said. She co-authored a new report showing that more than half of young people, between the ages of 13 and 27, gambled in the past year – and among the young gamblers, 39.5% had some degree of gambling-related risk and 10.3% were high risk for problem gambling.

Eisenberg’s research on online sports betting found that legalization is followed by measurable increases in treatment for depression and anxiety among young men. There have been some discussions after such findings to create state-level consumer protections – like deposit limits, self-exclusion, rules about advertising and funding for treatment paid out of state betting taxes, he said. “But the prediction markets sit outside all of that.” Very little of the revenue flows to states through taxes to support such treatment.
“In effect, these are gambling products that have exited the only regulatory system designed to limit gambling harm,” Eisenberg said.

Prediction markets are “really something that the government needs to clamp down on”, Nower said. Yet “the federal government still has no federal regulatory body,” she added. There are no research centers at the National Institutes of Health focused on gambling, as there are for alcohol and drug abuse.
“It’s just unaddressed at the federal level,” Nower said.
States like New Jersey are moving to restrict the markets – and concerns include consumer protection and the potential for insider trading, Nower said.
“People with inside information or control over an outcome could potentially profit from what they call ‘event contracts’,” another word for the predictions, she said.
This is the future, Eisenberg said: “Gambling on everything, everywhere, with fewer and fewer consumer protections.”

Yet he pointed out that public-health propositions on the markets were small, and he cautioned against seeing them as any sign of public sentiment. “Prices that small can be moved by a single trader and shouldn’t be read as public opinion,” Eisenberg said. “A few-hundred-dollar contract on the childhood vaccine schedule is not a forecast of anything.”
Within a week, the Polymarket sign in Brooklyn was vandalized. The bottom, with the Polymarket logo and the text on placing a prediction, was ripped away.
Now the sign simply reads: “Vaccines.”

articles.title: ‘Enough is enough’: rising number of deadly ebike battery fires spark fear in New York City
articles.summary:
City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year

Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters,…

blocks.text: Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat.

New York has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.

In late October, four members of a family, including an 11-year-old boy, died in a fire caused by a battery in an ebike that was in the pathway to an exit of an 11th floor apartment in a public housing building in the Bronx.

Then recently in a fire at a home in Brooklyn, six people died and nine were injured, including three firefighters and two police officers. Investigators discovered lithium-ion batteries at the scene but have not determined whether they caused the fire, the city council speaker, Julie Menin, said in a statement.
“The presence of lithium-ion batteries at the scene is a serious concern, and more must be done to encourage and mandate safe storage practices. Enough is enough,” Menin stated.
London and Toronto have also recently seen a dramatic increase in lithium-ion battery fires, which are often caused by overcharging and defective or damaged batteries.
Some of that trend is simply because ebikes, often used by food delivery workers and commuters, have become more popular.

blocks.caption: An ebike store was destroyed after a fire broke out inside the ground floor, in Brooklyn, on 18 February 2023.  Photograph: New York Daily News/NY Daily News/Getty Images

blocks.text: But in New York, the city has not executed its plan to build outdoor charging stations which would prevent people from plugging in the batteries in their apartments, where an overheated or defective battery poses a greater risk, experts say.

“There is a ton of red tape around this sort of new technology, and while it’s well intended to not let something new roll out too quickly, I think in this case, it is time to do something quickly,” said Laura Kavanagh, former commissioner of the FDNY.
In 2025, there were 2.2m ebikes imported into the United States, according to Light Electric Vehicle Association, double the number from just three years earlier.

In response to the increased usage and related increase in fires, the New York City department of transportation conducted a 2024 pilot in which it hired companies to offer battery-swapping cabinets where delivery workers could exchange exhausted batteries for charged ones.
The riders did more than 12,000 swaps over six months, and among participants, there was a 35% reduction in charging batteries at home, according to the city.
Following its success, the city announced that it would install 25 charging sites but not until 2027. The city first needed to “gather feedback on site selection, design and implementation”.
In April, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani asked residents to provide feedback on where they would like the 25 cabinets. The city planned to make them available in 2028, the announcement stated.
In 2023, the city also announced that it received a $25m federal grant to build 173 electric-micromobility charging and storage stations at 53 public housing developments.
“This means that residents will no longer need to charge their ebikes in their apartments, what we find to be extremely dangerous,” Mayor Eric Adams said at the time.
At the time, the deputy mayor, Meera Joshi, said residents would start “seeing evidence” of the stations in early 2024.
Three years later, none have been built.
Even though the Biden administration allocated the $25m for the infrastructure, the federal government has not actually provided the funds, according to the New York department of transportation.

Asked why the process has moved slowly, a transportation department spokesperson stated in an email: “The city’s strategy to reduce the risk e-bike battery fires focuses on getting unsafe devices off our streets and providing safe and convenient e-bike charging options” and the “outdoor battery swapping cabinets will make charging safer and more accessible for the thousands of delivery workers who rely on these devices to serve New Yorkers. With the public feedback we gathered this summer, we’re finalizing locations for our public e-bike charging program before advancing to the design phase and remain on pace to launch the service in 2028”.
Meanwhile, Popwheels, one of the companies in the successful pilot, has installed about 45 cabinets around the city, according to CEO Baruch Herzfeld.
He wants to install hundreds more around the city but has been stymied by a permitting process that he describes as “ludicrous”. He said it often takes six months for the city to approve one cabinet.

“If I want to put a cabinet that they approve in a parking lot, I have to use an architect to do a drawing, and then they have to come and do an inspection of a drawing of an ebike battery cabinet in the parking lot,” Herzfeld said. “This permitting process is why kids are dying.”

The city also often issues tickets to the owners of properties where Herzfeld has installed the cabinets, he said, for minor infractions like a fire extinguisher not having the proper tags or trash at the site.
Amanda Farinacci, the FDNY deputy commissioner public information, stated in an email that the tickets were not for “minor infractions but instead significant concerns”.

“The FDNY has been very serious partners with the micro-mobility/charging cabinet industry, being very accessible and collaborative to achieve solutions,” Farinacci stated. “We are a public safety agency and our mission is public safety. To conflate our regulatory responsibilities with causing people to charge their batteries indoors is entirely misplaced and inaccurate.”
Kavanagh, who spent a decade at FDNY before leaving in 2024, argued that the department is focusing on “too narrow of a concern”.

“I respect whatever concerns they have about the cabinet as real, but that is asking the wrong question,” said Kavanagh, who now works as a visiting urbanist at New York University. If “a battery failed in that cabinet outside, it is almost certain that would do no more than property damage. You are comparing that to” 10 New Yorkers dying in fires in the last three weeks.
“This is just appreciably worse, and so I think we need to frame it that way,” she added.

The latest fire may spur the city to expedite its approval process. On Friday, Menin announced that the city council would hold an emergency meeting on 20 November to conduct oversight to ensure the city is properly enforcing existing laws and that the public is educated on best fire safety practices and lithium-ion battery storage.

Ebike fires “are something that can cause people to lose their lives as well as their livelihoods”, Mamdani said on MS Now after the Brooklyn fire. “And so, we are really looking at every avenue we have to keep them safe.”

articles.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
articles.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

image.caption: Zelenskyy said he could put any comprehensive security deal to a public voteImage: Francisco Seco/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from its eastern region of ‌Donbas ⁠in exchange ⁠for joining NATO, according to remarks to the media published on Saturday.
The suggestion was made following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi to bring Russia's nearly 5-year war in Ukraine to a close.
What did Zelenskyy say?
The Ukrainian leader told reporters: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would ⁠Ukraine ​withdraw from Donbas?'"

Zelenskyy repeated Kyiv's position that it was not willing to cede territory to Russia. But he added that if the country reached a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, a ‌strong ​and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question ​to the public in a referendum.
"That ​is why ⁠I believe NATO is back on the ⁠agenda. ​But you have also heard [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Zelenskyy said the prospect of NATO membership in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas has not been raised before.
He also warned about Moscow's plan to change the continent's security architecture, saying it could lead to more conflict.
Putin has demanded that NATO pull back its troops from the Russian border, which European Union leaders have strongly criticized.
"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelenskyy added.
"Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe."
Europe chooses representatives for Ukraine peace talks
Europe to play bigger role in peace talks
On Friday, the EU said several European diplomats would take part in future Ukraine peace talks, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Poland.
Moscow has long insisted that European states be excluded from the negotiations because they support Ukraine.
Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia
The comments come as Russia’s Defence Ministry said its ⁠forces ⁠had captured the ​settlement of Tersianka in ​Ukraine’s southeastern ​Zaporizhzhia ‌region, news agency Interfax reported.

Interfax cited the ministry as saying that Russian ​forces had struck Ukrainian energy and ​transport infrastructure used by ⁠the ​military, along with ammunition ​depots and ​drone production ‌and storage sites.
Russia has targeted power stations across Ukraine in waves of ballistic and cruise missile attacks, cutting power and heating to millions of people as temperatures plunge.
Zelenskyy warned that Putin was "betting everything" on this winter's war campaign, which Kyiv insists is aimed at hurting public morale.

articles.title: New facilities in Laos and Cambodia: Is China expanding its military presence in Southeast Asia?
articles.summary: China has been growing its economic relationships in Southeast Asia. Now new military facilities in Laos and Cambodia are causing smaller countries to worry China's military networks are also…

image.caption: A Chinese soldier during joint maneuvers with Cambodia in May 2024Image: Heng Sinith/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: It's often said that maintaining good relations with your neighbors is essential. So in early November, China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi invited his counterparts from Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Myanmar to Beijing.
There the six countries agreed on closer economic and security cooperation.
The visit is just one example of China's growing influence on Southeast Asia. It's not just about trade or infrastructure either, it's also increasingly about military cooperation.
New airbase in Laos

For instance, at the end of September, China and Laos opened a joint military support and training center north of the Laotian capital, Vientiane. Initially Laotian air force pilots are to be trained at the Ban Keun airfield, China has said.

Earlier in 2025 China expanded its footprint at Cambodia's Ream naval base. China uses the facility on the Gulf of Thailand for logistics and training. And while Japanese and Vietnamese ships can visit the port, they're docked at a southern quay and it's unclear if other navies can use the same facilities under the same conditions as China.
"It remains to be seen how this [Ban Keun] will change China's military access to Southeast Asia," says Marco Bünte, a professor of Asian politics at the University Erlangen Nuremberg in Germany.

blocks.caption: A satellite image shows construction of Ban Keun airfield in LaosImage: Vantor/REUTERS

blocks.text: In recent years, China has significantly expanded its economic influence in the region.
The China-Laos railway and other infrastructure projects connect Laos more closely with its northern neighbor. Laos is also heavily indebted to China.
Bünte points out that Laos and Cambodia have been close military partners of China for some time and the new facility in Laos can be seen as another step towards deepening cooperation.
If that proves correct, "China would gain strategic depth in mainland Southeast Asia," Bünte explained. "It would also give China better military access to the South China Sea."

Johann Fuhrmann, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's Beijing office, points out that one should distinguish between training Laotian pilots and any potential use of the facilities by Chinese armed forces later.
"China gains influence when it co-designs the training and operation of such facilities over several years," Fuhrmann told DW.
Laos: A country in the grip of the Chinese?
Chinese planes in Laos

But nobody should underestimate China's military positioning, Bünte continued. "China is expanding its military operational capabilities here although I wouldn't speak of military hegemony because China hasn't achieved that yet."

With regard to the Laotian airbase, China says that Laotian pilots will be trained there. But beside military transporters and helicopters, Laos actually only has three light combat aircraft by Russia's Yakovlev works.

According to the aviation media outlet FlightGlobal, four more K-8s, Chinese two-seat intermediate jet trainer and light attack aircrafts, are in service there. Satellite images analyzed by the Reuters news agency in early October show eight K-8s at the base — even thought this doesn't necessarily mean they are stationed there permanently.
Fuhrmann doesn't think anybody should jump to conclusions about this.
"The idea of ​​a Chinese air corridor is more of a future scenario than something that has already been proven," he says.
For example, the runway at Ban Keun is only 2,000 meters (6,562 feet) long, which makes it too short for large Chinese bombers. These usually require 3,000 meters.

blocks.caption: A 2022 satellite image shows the Ream naval base in CambodiaImage: picture alliance/AP

blocks.text: The crucial question is what rights China will be granted, Fuhrmann continues: "Will China have to obtain the approval of the respective government for every new use? Or are there longer-term commitments that both sides can invoke, even in times of crisis?"
Surrounding countries are reacting differently to what appears to be China's growing influence in Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar because these countries are already considered closer to China.

Other Southeast Asian nations are hedging, trying to expand their relationship with China without severing ties with the US and also maintaining economic links with other Western nations. China's involvement offers them additional options and Beijing wants to explore those possibilities. That's just pragmatic though, Bünte says of the smaller Asian nations.
"Overall, these states… try to keep as many options open as possible," he notes.
China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific
China: 'Not against third parties'

Vietnam and the Philippines are watching developments particularly closely. Both have territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea. But Vietnam also has close historical ties to Laos and trained its own military there.

In early November, the Vietnamese government declared that any military cooperation must serve peace and stability and referred to the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast Asia, commonly known as the ASEAN Treaty. China is not an ASEAN member but has also stated that its activities are not directed against any third parties.
"So far, these are individual steps," Bünte adds. "We would have to wait and see if this leads to a broader military alliance in the years to come."
Fuhrmann says that Western nations should help strengthen the smaller countries in the region and take their interests seriously.
"Ultimately, a counterweight can only be achieved through tangible contributions, not through warnings or lectures from Europe," he says.
This story was originally published in German.

Economics experts are warning that the country is living beyond its means

blocks.text: This is a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on November 14, 2026:
November 14, 2026
Solar energy output set for record high in Germany in 2026

An above-average number of sunshine hours and the growing number of photovoltaic facilities has contributed to solar energy production that is approaching a record total for Germany, an industry association says.

By September 27, solar energy output had reached 90.2 terawatt-hours, which is already more than the 90 terawatt-hours generated for all of 2025, according to the German Solar Association (BSW -Solar) in Berlin.

That means that solar energy in net electricity generation in Germany is likely to reach a record level of more than 100 terawatt-hours in a single calendar year — almost 10 times the amount of electricity used by a major city like Hamburg in a year.
It is also almost 50 times as much as the 2.2 terawatt-hours generated byx solar power 20 years ago.
Carsten Körnig, the managing director of BSW-Solar, said the likely record was an important milestone as the world seeks to move away from climate-changing fossil fuels.
"Photovoltaics has developed from a niche technology into a cornerstone of our electricity supply," Körnig said.
"Society as a whole benefits from this: through cheaper electricity, fewer energy import and significantly lower climate-related damages," he said.
At 17.8% of total power generation, photovoltaics was the third most important energy source of domestically produced electricity behind wind power — the top energy source — followed by coal.

articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
articles.summary:
Tech company says services now restored to all customers and regions hit by one of worst IT failures in years

Microsoft has said its service is fully restored after a massive outage that…

blocks.text: Microsoft has said its service is fully restored after a massive outage that caused widespread disruption to governments, businesses and public services around the world.

The tech company said on Saturday morning it had restored service to the remaining customers affected by one of the worst IT failures in years. On its Microsoft 365 status page, the US-based firm said: “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.
“Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.”

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had affected some of their operations.
In the UK vital public services were hit, with hospital staff resorting to paper records and courtrooms scrambling to locate fax machines.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.
More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing at about midday on Thursday in the US and 6pm in the UK.

The Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents. It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” after a recent network change.

The disruptions offer the latest example of the cascading problems that can arise when so many communications and tech platforms depend on the same provider. The outage fuelled concerns in the UK about an over-reliance on a small number of tech companies.

Tim Clement-Jones, a former chair of the House of Lords artificial intelligence select committee, said the widespread outages of vital government services were an “I told you so moment” highlighting Britain’s dependence on US tech.
after newsletter promotion

Jeremy Singer, a professor at the University of Glasgow’s school of computing science, said: “This problem serves to emphasise the dependence we have built on one company’s digital infrastructure, and may lead us to question whether we need more resilience in our IT ecosystem.”
The global reach of the outage was swift. After problems first emerged Downdetector said it received outage reports from 74 countries and territories within an hour .
The total number of people affected was not clear, but Microsoft said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services.

articles.title: Torture survivors may have been sent to Sussex asylum camp unlawfully, documentary reveals
articles.summary:
Undercover ITV report also shows inadequate welfare checks at ex-military base run by firm of asylum camp billionaire Graham King

Asylum seekers accommodated at a controversial military base…

blocks.text: Asylum seekers accommodated at a controversial military base in East Sussex have been subjected to inadequate welfare checks, and torture survivors may have been placed there unlawfully, a new undercover documentary for ITV has revealed.

Mass accommodation sites are central to the government’s plan to end the use of hotels to house asylum seekers. For the documentary Inside The Asylum Camp, ITV’s undercover reporter got a job as a welfare officer at Crowborough and covertly filmed inside the former military training camp. The documentary claims that poor screening and welfare checks are having serious consequences for some of the asylum seekers.
Last May, the high court ruled that a Home Office policy change forcing torture survivors to share rooms was unlawful. The accommodation at Crowborough is in large dormitories.

The Home Office’s decision to accommodate asylum seekers on two former military sites – Crowborough, and Wethersfield in Essex – have triggered opposition from local residents. Plans to use three other sites – Bicester, Barnham and Linton-on-Ouse – have caused a similar outcry, mostly around fears about asylum seekers causing a rise in violent crime. However, very low levels of even minor crimes have been recorded by police at Wethersfield and Crowborough among asylum seekers at the two camps.

The Crowborough site is run by Clearsprings Ready Homes. According to its latest accounts, it is generating millions of pounds in income every day from its asylum accommodation contracts. Its boss, Graham King, has become the first asylum accommodation billionaire.

The documentary footage shows that, although two comprehensive welfare checks are supposed to be carried out each month by Clearsprings welfare officers, some staff appear to admit cutting corners and not asking all the questions they are required to ask of asylum seekers. On one occasion a welfare officer is filmed telling the undercover reporter “you don’t need to go in too deep”.
Staff appear to admit to falling behind on the 1,000 welfare checks they are supposed to carry out each month saying: “We’re so fucked.”

Concerns about an asylum seeker can be flagged on their file. A welfare officer is filmed telling the undercover reporter: “Those flags mean nothing” and that “nobody ever looks at them again”. When asked by the undercover reporter if some asylum seekers fall through the net due to brief welfare checks carried out, the welfare officer replies: “Oh, absolutely.”
The undercover reporter says he has identified four or five survivors of torture who should not have been sent to the military camp.

Louise Calvey, the executive director of the charity Asylum Matters, raised concerns about the findings of the undercover documentary. Her organisation has a campaign to accommodate asylum seekers in communities not camps. “The reports of torture survivors being accommodated on military barracks are appalling,” she said. “Brave survivors endure appalling experiences arriving to a country where they thought they’d be safe – a supposed civilised country, placing them in camps without the support they desperately need.
after newsletter promotion

“People being held in isolation for prolonged periods of time without access to sufficient water demonstrate just how far we have fallen as a country. That government contractors can fail so resoundingly in their duty of care to people seeking safety in our country demonstrates how much our system dehumanises refugees.”

Calvey said the government needed to urgently review its use of the camps, which she described as “a choice to punish people for having the audacity to exercise their lawful right to seek asylum here”.
The Home Office and Clearsprings have been approached.

articles.title: Greenpeace boulders may delay building of £12bn windfarms in North Sea
articles.summary:
Activists dumped rocks off Norfolk coast on site of Burnham-backed project in protest against seabed trawling

The

blocks.text: The giant offshore windfarms backed by Andy Burnham this week may face unexpected stumbling blocks after Greenpeace activists unwittingly dumped about 15 tonnes of boulders on to the site as part of a campaign against seabed trawling in the North Sea.

Greenpeace created the “boulder barrier” to safeguard harbour porpoises off the Norfolk coast by dropping giant stone blocks, each weighing up to 2 tonnes, on to the sea floor to prevent a method of fishing known as bottom trawling.

The barrier will pose an additional challenge for the green energy developers because most of the boulders were dropped on to the site earmarked for one of the UK’s biggest planned windfarms, known as the Norfolk Vanguard project.

blocks.caption: Greenpeace campaigners drop boulders onto the seabed to create anti-trawler barrier

blocks.text: Greenpeace began dumping boulders on to the site, without consent from the marine authority, days before the prime minister told the Cop31 summit that the UK would invest £1bn of public money in the Vanguard West and Vanguard East windfarms in what is believed to be the biggest investment of its kind in UK history.
The Guardian understands that Greenpeace checked the seabed for any existing cables, pipelines or shipwrecks, but it was not aware of the plans to build the Vanguard East windfarm.

The creation of the underwater barrier in one of “the most heavily trawled” areas of the southern North Sea was timed to coincide with the premiere of the BBC’s Blue Planet III documentary, narrated by Sir David Attenborough.
Some boulders bear the signatures of celebrities including Simon Pegg and Benedict Cumberbatch, who have voiced marine conservation documentaries, and agreed to support the Greenpeace campaign.

However, they are likely to be removed within months after renewable energy developers agreed a £12bn deal alongside the UK government to begin building the offshore windfarm next year. Industrial fishing activities, including bottom trawling, are also likely to move elsewhere to avoid the construction area.

The Guardian understands that the offshore wind developer, the German utility company RWE, is in talks with Greenpeace to verify the exact placement of the boulders so that they can update the seabed surveys they began last summer. The company is also investigating any potential impact to the construction of the project or its undersea cables.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Greenpeace crew and activists next to a boulder with a carved depiction of David Attenborough while aboard the Greenpeace ship Arctic Sunrise this month. Photograph: Suzanne Plunkett/Reuters

blocks.text: A spokesperson for RWE described its communication with Greenpeace as “constructive” and said the company would “continue to investigate the precise implications” for the Norfolk Vanguard East project.
Will McCallum, the co-executive director of Greenpeace UK, said any suggestion that the boulders would cause a genuine obstacle was “absurd”.
“Anyone familiar with offshore wind in the North Sea knows that energy companies routinely move naturally occurring boulders from the seabed before building windfarms,” he said.
“Some of these boulders can be 10 times heavier than those we placed.

“Greenpeace has long championed offshore wind and will continue to do so. While we wait for this windfarm to be built, our boulders will provide an essential barrier to destructive bottom trawlers that are decimating the seabed in this protected area.”

Concerns were raised about the environmental impact of Pax Silica and its potential to displace Indigenous peoples and farming communities, with students questioning who benefits from the initiative.

Despite the protests, the Philippine government clarified that the Pax Silica agreement would not be signed during the ASEAN Summit, urging for more constructive discussions rather than demonstrations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Thousands of students from different parts of the Philippines staged protests on Friday, November 13, against the US-led Pax Silica initiative and US President Donald Trump’s expected arrival in the country for the ASEAN Summit.
Filipinos have raised concerns about the initiative’s potential environmental impact and the possible displacement of indigenous peoples and farming communities.
In Manila, students from the University of Santo Tomas (UST), Asia’s oldest Catholic university, walked out of their classrooms to join the protest.

“Pax Silica is reported to generate hundreds of thousands of indirect and induced jobs. However, projections are not promises and promises are not guarantees, especially when dealing with a global power like the United States,” the UST Central Student Council Executive Board said.
“It is not enough to ask what development Pax Silica can offer; we must also ask who stands to benefit from it, and more importantly, who will bear its costs,” it added.
At De La Salle University, at least 1,500 students also walked out of their classrooms to protest against the initiative.

blocks.caption: STUDENT PROTEST. Students from De La Salle University’s Manila Campus walk out of their classes on November 13, 2026, in protest of Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump’s visit for the upcoming ASEAN Summit. Photo by Zara Pineda/Rappler

blocks.text: Students from different campuses of the University of the Philippines, Polytechnic University of the Philippines, Miriam College, and Ateneo de Manila University also joined the demonstrations.

blocks.caption: RALLY. University of the Philippines Manila students stage a snake rally at the College of Arts and Sciences in accordance with the UP system-wide walkout on November 13, 2026. Photo by Axel Cainglet/Rappler

blocks.text: In Benguet, around 9,000 students from various schools, including UP Baguio, Saint Louis University, and the University of the Cordilleras took to the streets to express their opposition to Pax Silica.

blocks.caption: Thousands of students protest vs Pax Silica, Trump’s arrival in Manila

blocks.text: Students from Central Luzon State University also staged a protest on Thursday, November 12.
The signing of the Pax Silica agreement had reportedly been targeted for November, coinciding with Trump’s visit to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit.
However, Department of Trade and Industry Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo clarified that the Philippines would not sign the agreement during the 49th ASEAN Summit.
“We do not want to distract attention or take away attention from the regional initiatives that ASEAN and the Philippines are proposing,” Rodolfo told reporters on Tuesday, November 10.
Amid the protests, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro appealed to the public to reconsider holding demonstrations during the summit.

“’Kung ano man ang panawagan ito ay sana hindi dinadaan sa pagprotesta although ito ay kanilang karapatan. Pero sa panahon ngayon mas magandang nagkakaroon ng mas masinsinang paguusapan kung ano man ang concerns ng mga estudyante,” Castro said during a press briefing on Saturday, November 14.

(Whatever their demands may be, I hope these are not pursued through protests, although I recognize that this is their right. In these times, however, it would be better to have more in-depth discussions about whatever concerns the students may have.)
Different groups are also expected to stage protests in different parts of the country in succeeding days, coinciding with the ASEAN Summit. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
articles.summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.

blocks.text: Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said.

Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister's 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing.
Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive.
On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash - found in secluded locations across the country - Magyar described it as the end of the "mafia".

Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement.
The cash amounted to "5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100", it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said.
The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory".
Magyar promised Hungarians "regime change" during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office.
Allegations of corruption and cronyism have long dogged Orbán, who during the course of his tenure turned Hungary into what the EU characterised as an "electoral autocracy".

articles.title: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president says US envoys touted the exchange as part of efforts to end the war with Russia.

blocks.text: US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The Ukrainian president's comments on Saturday come after US envoys visited Moscow and an EU summit in Dublin as part of ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance as a condition of any peace deal to deter future threats, while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable.
Zelensky has also consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory, despite Moscow's demands for it to cede the Donbas.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow the day prior.

Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider.
Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.

There have, however, been recent signs the two can find common ground: last month, US First Lady Melania Trump was able to broker a temporary ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky to allow for evacuations and aid deliveries.
US officials had previously said that Ukrainian Nato membership was off the table.
Zelensky said on Saturday that the US proposal made him believe that "Nato is back on the agenda".
But he cautioned: "You have also heard Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.

Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be a small concession in practical terms, but would be symbolically significant for Kyiv because it would constitute an acceptance of the Donbas being Russian.
Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine's regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014.

articles.title: 5 Philippine creative cities team up to make UNESCO badge count
articles.summary: Baguio, Cebu, Iloilo, Dumaguete, and Quezon City hope to turn global recognition into real support for local artists, educators, and communities

items: Representatives from the Philippines' UNESCO Creative and Learning Cities gathered in Baguio to strengthen cooperation and enhance opportunities for artists and communities.
A Pledge of Cooperation was established among the five Creative Cities, focusing on resource sharing, joint initiatives, and promoting creative communities, particularly for women.
Discussions highlighted the importance of connecting creativity with education, addressing challenges in sustaining creative industries, and preserving cultural identity through community engagement.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
BAGUIO CITY, Philippines – Being recognized by UNESCO is one thing. Making that recognition work for artists, cultural workers, educators, and ordinary communities is another.

This was the challenge confronting representatives of the Philippines’ UNESCO Creative and Learning Cities who gathered in Baguio from November 5 to 8, and agreed to strengthen cooperation beyond the international distinctions their cities have earned.

The gathering, organized by the UNESCO National Commission of the Philippines (UNACOM) and the Baguio City government, brought together the country’s five UNESCO Creative Cities: Baguio for Crafts and Folk Art, Cebu for Design, Iloilo for Gastronomy, Quezon City for Film, and Dumaguete for Literature.
Representatives of the UNESCO Learning Cities of Balanga, Baguio, Legazpi, and Quezon City also participated, linking creative industries with education, lifelong learning, and community development.
Held alongside the ninth IBAGIW Baguio Creative Festival, the convergence was part of UNACOM’s 75th anniversary activities.
At the center of the gathering was a Pledge of Cooperation among the five Creative Cities, witnessed and supported by Learning City representatives.

The pledge commits the cities to sharing resources and expertise, pursuing joint initiatives, and promoting their creative communities nationally and internationally. It also seeks to expand opportunities for women, including access to creative spaces, leadership positions, and industry resources.
The agreement builds on the Philippine Creative Industries Development Act, which provides a national framework for supporting creative enterprises and cultural workers.
Baguio Mayor Benjamin Magalong, whose city became the country’s first UNESCO Creative City in 2017, said international recognition should be measured by the opportunities it creates.
“Bilang kauna-unahang lungsod sa Pilipinas na napabilang sa UNESCO Creative Cities Network noong 2017, naniniwala tayo na ang pagkilala ay hindi lamang isang karangalan,” Magalong said.

“Mas mahalaga ang mga oportunidad na nalilikha nito para sa ating mga artists, artisans, cultural workers, educators, at mga komunidad na patuloy na nagpapanatili ng ating kultura at pagkakakilanlan.”

(As the first city in the Philippines to be included in the UNESCO Creative Cities Network in 2017, we believe that this recognition is not merely an honor. More important are the opportunities it creates for our artists, artisans, cultural workers, educators, and the communities that continue to preserve our culture and identity.)

The meeting also examined how cooperation could address challenges that individual cities face in sustaining their creative industries, from access to markets and training to the preservation of traditional knowledge.
Creative Baguio City Council co-convenor Marie Venus Tan stressed the importance of connecting creativity with learning and preserving Filipino cultural identity.
Paolo Mercado, president of the Creative Economy Council of the Philippines, argued that creative education must extend beyond the arts.
“Creative thinking is not just artistic thinking; it is also scientific thinking because it is innovation,” Mercado said.
The discussions took a more community-focused turn on November 6, when UNACOM and Baguio City held a consultation on expanding learning opportunities for women and girls.

Participants examined the contributions of indigenous women and traditional knowledge holders to cultural preservation, while identifying barriers to education, resources, leadership, and decision-making.

On November 7, Creative City representatives also agreed to approach the Department of Trade and Industry through the Philippine Creative Industry Development Council to seek support for their continued participation in international UNESCO activities and networks.
They discussed possible joint projects, partnerships between cities, and exchanges that could benefit artists, artisans, and creative enterprises.
The delegates’ visit to Baguio offered examples of how these ideas could work beyond conference rooms.
They toured creative spaces and community enterprises, including the BenCab Museum, Asin Road woodcarving establishments, Ili-likha, Pilak, Mandëko Kito, and other venues participating in IBAGIW.
Learning City representatives also visited Vivita Philippines, a learning space where young people develop ideas through hands-on experimentation, design, and creative problem-solving.
The visits brought attention to the practical challenges of sustaining traditional crafts, creating livelihoods, and passing cultural knowledge to younger generations.
National Artist Kidlat Tahimik, speaking during the festival’s opening ceremonies, cautioned against measuring development solely through economic indicators.

“Now, we always equate progress with the quantifiables. Nakakalimutan na natin ang (We forget the) soul of the city,” he said, referring to the knowledge inherited from ancestors and elders that cannot easily be measured but remains important to the future.
UNACOM deputy executive director Lindsay Barrientos commended Baguio for translating its UNESCO designation into local programs but called for stronger systems of cooperation among cities.

The next test for the newly strengthened network will be turning its commitments into actual projects, with participating cities expected to pursue partnerships, seek institutional support, and expand opportunities for their creative communities.
The IBAGIW Baguio Creative Festival continues throughout November with exhibitions, performances, artisan fairs, workshops, and other cultural activities across the city. – Rappler.com

items: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's state visit to the Philippines marks the beginning of a new era in diplomatic relations, coinciding with the 80th anniversary of their ties.
Lula emphasized the importance of collaboration on political reforms, particularly in the UN and WTO, and highlighted shared values between Brazil and the Philippines.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. described Lula's visit as a significant milestone, aiming to strengthen cooperation in regional and multilateral platforms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said on Saturday, November 14, that his state visit to the Philippines is expected to usher in a “new age of relations” between the two countries who are marking their 80th year of diplomatic ties this year.

Lula, the first Brazilian president to go on a state visit to the Philippines, said this at the start of his expanded bilateral meeting with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit, which the Philippines chairs.

“This visit to the Philippines, may it be the start of a new age of relations between Brazil and the Philippines. But a new age not just trade-wise but also a new age in politics as we have very common ideas and thoughts in relation to the need for reforming the UN, in advocating for multilateralism, in the recovery of the WTO, and strengthening UN institutions also at the same time,” he said.

blocks.caption: Lula: Philippine state visit start of ‘new age of relations’ with Brazil

blocks.text: “We are also very much interested in reforming the UN Security Council for us to give United Nations the necessary credibility once more of an institution that may work to ensure peace in the world,” Lula added.
Marcos, in his statement, cited Lula’s visit as a “high point” of the 80th year of Philippines-Brazil ties.

The Philippine leader noted that the two countries share many commonalities. “In the international arena, we stand shoulder to shoulder in advocating for an international order grounded on dialogue, cooperation and international law,” Marcos added.
At the state luncheon in honor of Lula, Marcos called his visit a “watershed moment” for their countries.
“I hope to enhance our cooperation in regional and multilateral fronts such as the United Nations and in ASEAN,” Marcos said.

articles.title: Ombudsman Remulla: DFA should not have authority over passports
articles.summary: Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday renewed his criticism of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), saying passport issuance should not be under the agency's authority.

blocks.text: Published November 14, 2026 6:02pm
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla on Saturday renewed his criticism of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), saying passport issuance should not be under the agency's authority.
Remulla previously proposed outsourcing visa issuance to a third party, a suggestion that the DFA rejected.
“Ang visa giving, tsaka ang passport, ang passport, that is all the function of immigration,” Remulla said on his dzRH radio program.
(Visa issuance and passports should all be under the functions of the Bureau of Immigration.)

“Dapat passporting, pag-isipan na natin. Huwag na natin ilagay sa DFA… Mas mabuti ‘yan, yung Passport Act, we should repeal it and just go back to the very basic. To guard our borders, it has to be immigration,” he added.

(We should rethink the passport issuance process. Let us not put it under the DFA. It would be better to repeal the Passport Act and go back to the basics. Border protection should be handled by immigration.)
Remulla said that in some European countries, the police grant visa extensions because the matter falls under law enforcement.

He also raised concerns over alleged cases of fake Filipinos obtaining legitimate Philippine passports, while genuine Filipino citizens struggle to secure passport appointments, with some having to travel long distances to get their documents.
The Ombudsman again raised concerns over Chinese travelers overstaying in the Philippines under the country's visa-free entry policy.
While acknowledging the need to support the tourism sector, Remulla said the policy also raised security concerns involving China.
Remulla maintained that passport and visa issuance should be treated as law enforcement matters.
“Ang function talaga ng DFA ngayon in this day and age, number one is diplomacy. Number two is assistance to Filipinos. The rest, forget it. Wala na,” Remulla said.
(The DFA's primary function in this day and age is diplomacy. Second is providing assistance to Filipinos. The rest, forget it. There is no need for anything else.)
GMA News Online has sought comment from the DFA and will update this story once it responds. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Snowbirds set to fly iconic jets for last time this weekend
articles.summary: Fifty-five years after the team's formation, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' iconic jets will grace the skies one last time. The aerobatics team's CT-114 Tutor jets are set to fly over Calgary's…

image.caption: The Snowbirds during a practice run ahead of the Canadian International Air Show along the Toronto lakeshore on Sept. 4, 2026. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Calgary

Fifty-five years after the team's formation, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' iconic jets will grace the skies one last time. The aerobatics team's CT-114 Tutor jets are set to fly over Calgary's McMahon Stadium on Sunday as part of the 113th Grey Cup festivities, before being grounded permanently.
CT-114 Tutor jets will fly over Calgary this Sunday before retirement
Fifty-five years after the team's formation, the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' iconic jets will grace the skies one last time.
The aerobatics team's CT-114 Tutor jets are set to fly over Calgary's McMahon Stadium on Sunday as part of the 113th Grey Cup festivities, before being grounded permanently.
Aviation enthusiast Jesse Millington wouldn't miss the legendary squadron's final flight for the world.

"I can't wait for it. I was fortunate enough to see them out in Abbotsford this year, and I didn't know if I'd get another chance to actually see them fly," said Millington, who's coming to Calgary from Foothills County for the event.
"Through my entire life the Snowbirds have always just been there," Millington said.
He parked this plane in his backyard to preserve Alberta's aviation history
The CAF ordered the team's signature CT-114 Tutor jets as training aircraft in 1961.
Since then, they've been used in performances across North America.
"It's one of the most Canadian things," Millington said. "It's like hockey. You could say it's like Tim Hortons and all the rest."

The federal government announced in May that the CT-114 Tutor jets would be retired after the 2026 flying season. They're set to be replaced by Swiss-made CT-157 Siskin II planes, but those won't be here until the 2030s at the earliest.
A file photo of a CT-114 Tutor jet used by the Canadian Forces Snowbirds. (Tom Ayers/CBC)

Millington says he has "mixed emotions" on this being the last flight of the Snowbirds, but he's glad he and fellow aviation enthusiasts — both in Calgary and tuning in virtually from around the world — will get to experience the historic occasion.
"The best part is that they're going out in a very Canadian style and lots of people get to see this," he said.
Snowbirds crew members look ahead
Maj. Steve Sparks, who flies with the squadron as Snowbird 6, says the final flight on Sunday will be an emotional one.
"I felt it a few times this season in flights, knowing that it's coming to an end," he said.

items: Snowbirds prepare to say goodbye to iconic 63-year-old jets in final airshow
A city between flights: How Moose Jaw is holding on to the Snowbirds

blocks.text: Sparks, who grew up playing football, says he's grateful to be part of the Canadian Football League championship festivities in Calgary.
"From a young kid dreaming of playing in the Grey Cup one day, I get to do it a different way now," Sparks said.
Canadian Forces Snowbirds members Master Cpl. Triston Popescu, left, and Maj. Steve Sparks on Nov. 13, 2026. (CBC)
Master Cpl. Triston Popescu, the squadron's maintenance deputy crew chief, says the moment "is bittersweet" but the future is bright.
"I've had a lot of memories, a lot of adventures, met a lot of amazing people, and actually performed in front of a lot of amazing venues and crowds," he said.
Snowbirds take their final flight over Toronto until the 2030s at annual air show
Popescu says transitioning to the new jet model is part of what makes the moment so bittersweet, as he's been working with the current model for more than a decade.
"Going to a new aircraft later on is going to be a little bit of a transition for everybody, but I feel that's the right direction," he said.

Amir Said is a multimedia journalist with CBC Calgary. He is an alumnus of the University of Regina, and his award-winning work as a writer and photographer has been published by outlets across Canada, including Postmedia, The Hill Times and The Narwhal. articles.title: Experts warn about risks of AI-generated content in child sexual abuse material
articles.summary: Prince Edward Island RCMP say there has been a "notable increase" in child sex abuse material made using artificial intelligence across parts of the province. Online exploitation specialists say this…

image.caption: P.E.I. RCMP estimate one third of all investigations including child sexual abuse material now include AI-generated content. (Shutterstock)

blocks.text: WARNING: This story contains disturbing descriptions of child sex abuse. Resources and supports for anyone who has experienced sexual violence can be found at the bottom of this story.

Prince Edward Island RCMP say there has been a "notable increase" in child sex abuse material made using artificial intelligence across parts of the province. Online exploitation specialists say this surge in illegal AI-generated content could be growing the demand for real-world child abuse.
Internet watchdog reports indicate a trending global rise in AI-generated child sex abuse content, previously known as child pornography.
In an email, P.E.I. RCMP senior communications adviser Scott Ferris said it’s a "safe estimate" that one third of Island RCMP online child abuse investigations now involve AI-generated material.
That estimate considers only areas under RCMP jurisdiction, which excludes Charlottetown, Summerside and Kensington.
LISTEN | How criminals are using AI to abuse children:
This is PEI23:45How criminals are using AI to abuse children
AI child exploitation cases are surfacing across the Atlantic region.

In St. John’s, N.L., this summer, a 17-year-old boy was charged with nearly 60 counts related to the creation and distribution of child sexual abuse material. Police allege he used AI tools to alter images of 19 minors and make them explicit.

Const. Stephanie Myers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary told CBC News On the Go host Krissy Holmes the case is "probably one of our first if not the first" specifically involving AI being used to create child sexual exploitation material.

A 17-year-old in St John's, N.L., faces 58 charges related to his alleged use of AI to alter images of teenagers. Const. Stephanie Myers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) says this is likely one of the RNC's first AI-specific child abuse cases. (Danny Arsenault/CBC)
What is AI-generated child sexual abuse material?

Technological developments have dramatically changed how child sex abuse crimes are committed. With AI, criminals no longer need to make direct contact with an underage victim to create new abusive content.
But that doesn’t mean these are victimless crimes.

items: AI-generated material found in one-third of P.E.I. RCMP online child abuse cases
Police say 19 victims identified in AI child sexual abuse image investigation

blocks.text: "In many of the cases … AI-generated content is either produced to create material of a child that’s in the family or the neighbourhood of that offender," said Mauranne Ste-Marie, senior research analyst with the national RCMP’s sensitive and specialized investigative services unit.
"It increases the demand for the material, it normalizes the abuse."

Certain generative AI models — which are ultimately trained on images of real people — can create abusive images or videos either in the likeness of a specific person or by generating a non-existent, synthetic child from scratch.
Some offenders also use AI-powered "nudify" tools to create explicit "deepfakes" — realistic fake images or videos of a victim.
'Nudify' apps and AI-generated child sex abuse material are on the rise. Here’s what you can do about it
"Anyone can take pictures that are posted online ... take the face of your children and create very graphic sexual abuse material with it," Ste-Marie told CBC News.

“There are virtually no limits to what can be produced.... If their sexual preferences are for young girls with blond hair, blue eyes, they don’t need to spend time searching for that preference online anymore. They can simply create it."

Mainstream generative AI models like ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude have strict safeguards in place that are designed to block the generation of any child abuse material. Confirmed violations are supposedly then reported to law enforcement.
To circumvent these controls, offenders often rely on freely available open-source software to generate abusive media offline, where is it far harder to detect.
Since these models are typically used without an internet connection, any exploitative content they produce can be incredibly difficult for police to track.
Ste-Marie warned using generative AI models this way could lead to more real-world abuse.
"It is a stepping stone, it is one step closer to sexually abusing a child," she said.
"After viewing material for a certain number of weeks or months, it may not meet their needs anymore."
Sextortion
In an email, Summerside police reported at least one instance where a suspect used AI-generated child sex abuse material in a "sextortion" attempt this year.
Sextortion is a form of online blackmail where offenders coerce victims into sending money or explicit media by threatening to release sensitive images or videos.
In April 2023, 17-year-old Harry Burke from Fortune Bridge, P.E.I., tragically took his own life hours after telling his parents he had been victimized by a sextortion scam.
Carl Burke and Barbie Lavers hold up a photo of their son, Harry Burke. He took his own life after being victimized by a sextortion attempt. (Laura Meader/CBC)

Jacques Marcoux, director of research for the Canadian Centre for Child Protection, said AI-generated or manipulated material is increasingly used in sextortion attempts. His organization operates Cybertip.ca, Canada’s national tip line for reporting online child abuse.

"In lieu of being able to trick the child into giving them an intimate image, they’ll simply create one using AI," Marcoux said, noting that offenders then threaten to release images online, claiming that they're real.
P.E.I. RCMP media relations officer Gavin Moore said there were 26 reported instances of sextortion last year in Island areas under RCMP jurisdiction.
Moore didn’t specifically reference AI-generated material in any of these cases, but he did note reporting rates are typically "very low" for this type of crime.
"This is a type of crime that victims are extremely embarrassed [about]," Moore told CBC News.
"[It] can have very devastating and significant effects on its victims."
As AI tools become more sophisticated, it’s getting harder to tell what’s real and what’s not, said Marcoux.
Jacques Marcoux, director of research and analytics at the Canadian Centre for Child Protection, says its getting more and more difficult to tell what's AI and what's not. (Jeff Stapleton/CBC)
"Unlike three years ago … you can’t discern whether or not it’s real in many cases. It’s almost a coin flip," Marcoux said.
But, from a legal standpoint, it doesn’t matter.

Under the criminal code, AI-generated child abuse is treated the same as authentic abuse material. Altering or generating explicit media with AI through written prompts can constitute making child sexual abuse material.
Police in St. John’s, N.L., applied that standard this summer.
The 17-year-old boy, who was hit with 58 criminal charges, faces 19 counts of making child sexual exploitation material after allegedly using AI to digitally alter photos of teenage girls.
What can you do?
Since offenders can now use AI tools to create abusive material based on any image, Ste-Marie warns there is always a risk involved when posting children online.

"Every time you post a picture or a video of yourself or your children, there is a risk that it could be used by someone with bad intentions," she said, noting that one recommendation is to take precautions like covering a child's face in photos.

items: Edmonton teens charged with using AI to create sexually exploitative images of classmates
2 charged over violent, sexual AI deepfakes of dozens of Canadian women

blocks.text: "The more images and information that are publicly available about a person, the easier it is for that model to create very convincing fake or manipulated content," Ste-Marie said.
"So, as soon as you reduce that availability, it makes it more difficult to create that type of content."
Although she said people can reduce the risk of being victimized, she stressed that online child abuse is never the victim’s fault.
"Your child is never responsible for the creation of that type of content, even if they posted images online and they feel like it was their fault, it never is," Ste-Marie said.
"They have the right to post and to share without thinking that someone will use it against them."
If you or someone you know has experienced sexual violence here’s where to get help:

items: Victim Services P.E.I.: Queens and Kings County: 902-368-4582; Prince County: 902-888-8218.
Rise P.E.I.: Phone or text: 902-218-6143.

Report Child Abuse: daytime 1-877-341-3101; after hours 1-800-341-6868.
You can check out a list of support services, programs, and other information on the 211 website or call 211 to be directed to the help you need.
